blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein humne seekha ke sequence kya hai aur \(a_{n}\) ka matlab kya hai. Ab do sawal: kya har sequence kabhi khatam hoti hai? Aur agar \(a_{n}\) ka formula diya ho to terms kaise nikalte hain? Is sabaq mein inhi dono sawalon ke jawab hain.

blocks.title: Numbering note
blocks.text: Kitab is heading ko 6.1.2 chhapti hai (kitab mein 6.1.1 kahin nahin); tarteeb barqarar rakhne ke liye portal isay 6.1.1 likhta hai.

items: A sequence which consists of a finite number of terms is called a finite sequence. For example, \(2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23\) is a finite sequence of 8 terms.

A sequence which consists of an infinite number of terms is called an infinite sequence. For example, \(3, 10, 17, 24, \ldots\) is an infinite sequence, or more generally \(3, 10, 17, 24, \ldots, 7n-4, \ldots\), to show how each term was generated.

blocks.text: Asaan alfaaz mein: finite sequence (mehdood silsila) woh hai jis ki terms ginti mein mehdood hon, yani kahin ruk jaye. Kitab ki misaal \(2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23\) mein poori 8 terms hain aur 23 par khatam. Infinite sequence (la-mehdood silsila) woh hai jo kabhi khatam na ho, jaise \(3, 10, 17, 24, \ldots\). Aakhir ke teen nuqte "\(\ldots\)" ka matlab hai "isi tarah hamesha chalta rahega". Kitab isay \(3, 10, 17, 24, \ldots, 7n-4, \ldots\) bhi likhti hai taa ke saaf dikh jaye ke har term kaise banti hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Pehchan ka aasan tareeqa: finite sequence ki aakhri term likhi hoti hai; infinite ke aakhir mein "\(\ldots\)" hote hain aur koi aakhri term nahin.
Rozmarra ki misaal: ek hafte ke saat din finite list hai (7 ke baad khatam), jab ke natural numbers \(1, 2, 3, \ldots\) kabhi khatam nahin hote.
\(7n - 4\) kahan se aaya? \(3, 10, 17, 24\) mein har term pichli se 7 zyada hai, is liye rule mein \(7n\) aayega. Ab \(n = 1\) par term 3 chahiye: \(7(1) = 7\), aur \(7 - 4 = 3\), is liye \(-4\). Tasdeeq: \(7(2) - 4 = 10\), \(7(3) - 4 = 17\), \(7(4) - 4 = 24\).
Kyun general term list ke andar likhte hain? Kyun ke sirf chaar terms dekh kar koi aur rule bhi socha ja sakta hai; \(7n - 4\) likhne se shak khatam ho jata hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: If a sequence is given, then we can find its \(n\)th term, and if the \(n\)th term of a sequence is given, then we can find the terms of the sequence.
Yeh Note do tarfa raasta batata hai: terms se formula, aur formula se terms. Formula se terms nikalna aasan hissa hai, isi se shuru karte hain. Kitab ki misaal dekhiye.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.problem: Find the first four terms of the sequences whose \(n\)th terms are given. (i) \(a_{n} = 3n + 1\) (ii) \(a_{n} = 3n^{2} - 3\)
steps:
Given: (i) \(a_{n} = 3n + 1\); (ii) \(a_{n} = 3n^{2} - 3\).
To find: har sequence ki pehli chaar terms \(a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, a_{4}\).
Method: sab se pehle samajhte hain ke \(a_{n}\) ek mashine ki tarah hai: position \(n\) daalo, term bahar aa jati hai. Is liye bas \(n = 1, 2, 3, 4\) baari baari rakhna hai.

Step 1: (i) \(a_{n} = 3n + 1\) mein \(n = 1\) rakhein
\[a_{1} = 3(1) + 1 = 4\]
Kyun: \(a_{1}\) pehli position wali term hai, is liye \(n\) ki jagah 1 aayega. \(3(1)\) ka matlab \(3 \times 1\) hai.

Step 2: (i) \(n = 2, 3, 4\) rakhein
\[a_{2} = 3(2) + 1 = 7\]
\[a_{3} = 3(3) + 1 = 10\]
\[a_{4} = 3(4) + 1 = 13\]
Kyun: rule wahi rehta hai, sirf position badalti hai. Pehli chaar terms: \(4, 7, 10, 13\).
Dhyan dein: har term pichli se 3 zyada hai, kyun ke \(n\) ek barhta hai to \(3n\) teen barhta hai.

Step 3: (ii) \(a_{n} = 3n^{2} - 3\) mein \(n = 1\) rakhein
\[a_{1} = 3(1)^{2} - 3 = 0\]
Kyun: yahan tarteeb zaroori hai: pehle \(n\) ka square, phir 3 se multiply, phir 3 minus. Power hamesha multiply se pehle lagti hai.

Tasdeeq:
(i) terms har baar 3 barh rahi hain (\(4, 7, 10, 13\)), jo \(3n\) se bilkul mel khata hai.
(ii) \(a_{n} = 3(n^{2} - 1)\) likh kar dekhein: \(n = 1, 2, 3, 4\) par \(3 \times 0, 3 \times 3, 3 \times 8, 3 \times 15\), yani \(0, 9, 24, 45\). Jawab durust hai.

blocks.text: Is misaal se ek sabaq aur milta hai: formula se terms nikalna sirf substitution hai, magar har qadam par order of operations (pehle bracket, phir power, phir zarb, phir jama/tafreeq) ka khayal rakhna zaroori hai. Exam mein aksar isi jagah number katte hain, is liye har term ko alag line mein likhiye.
Ab ek ahem baat. Jo sequences kisi khaas pattern par chalti hain unhein progressions (taraqqi pazeer silsile) kehte hain. Pattern ke hisaab se kitab inhein teen qismon mein taqseem karti hai:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Teeno ki ek jhalak (har ek ka apna section aage aayega):
Arithmetic: har baar ek fixed number jama hota hai, jaise \(5, 11, 17, 23, \ldots\) (6 jama).
Geometric: har baar ek fixed number se multiply hota hai, jaise \(6, 12, 24, 48, \ldots\) (2 se zarb).
Harmonic: terms ke reciprocals (ulte, jaise 2 ka \(\frac{1}{2}\)) arithmetic progression banate hain, jaise \(1, \frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{3}, \ldots\), kyun ke \(1, 2, 3, \ldots\) arithmetic hai.
Kyun yeh baant zaroori hai? Har qism ke apne formulas hain; sawal dekh kar pehle qism pehchanein, phir sahi formula lagayein.
Example 1 ki sequence (i) arithmetic hai. Sequence (ii) yani \(0, 9, 24, 45\) in teenon mein se koi nahin, kyun ke na us ke farq \(9, 15, 21\) barabar hain na ratios.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
1. \(1, 4, 9, 16, \ldots, 100\) finite hai ya infinite? (Finite: aakhri term 100 likhi hai.)
2. \(a_{n} = 2n - 1\) ki pehli teen terms? (Jawab: \(1, 3, 5\).)
3. \(5, 10, 20, 40, \ldots\) kaun si progression hai? (Geometric, har baar 2 se zarb.)

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin.) \(a_{n} = n^{2} + 1\) ki pehli chaar terms:
\[a_{1} = 1 + 1 = 2\]
\[a_{2} = 4 + 1 = 5\]
\[a_{3} = 9 + 1 = 10\]
\[a_{4} = 16 + 1 = 17\]
Terms: \(2, 5, 10, 17\). Farq \(3, 5, 7\) barabar nahin, is liye yeh arithmetic progression nahin; magar sequence zaroor hai kyun ke rule saaf hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Finite sequence ki aakhri term hoti hai; infinite sequence "\(\ldots\)" ke saath kabhi khatam nahin hoti.
2. Terms di hon to \(n\)th term nikal sakte hain; \(n\)th term diya ho to koi bhi term nikal sakte hain.
3. Term nikalne ke liye \(a_{n}\) mein \(n\) ki jagah position rakhiye, \(n = 1\) se shuru.
4. Progressions teen qism ki hain: arithmetic, geometric aur harmonic.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Power ko ghalat jagah lagana: \(3(4)^{2} = 48\) hai, \(144\) nahin.
2. \(n = 0\) se shuru kar dena: pehli term \(a_{1}\) hai, is liye \(n = 1\) se shuru karein.
3. Lambi list ko infinite samajh lena: jis list ki aakhri term likhi ho woh finite hai, chahe kitni bhi lambi ho.
4. Sirf do terms dekh kar progression ki qism tay kar lena: kam az kam teen terms ke farq aur ratio dono check karein.
